All four test methods call `runLtrExplainTest`, which in turn calls `createLtrIndex` using the same constant `LTR_SEARCH_INDEX`. In an `internalCluster()`-based integration test the cluster persists across test methods within the same class, so the second (and subsequent) test will fail when `prepareCreate(LTR_SEARCH_INDEX)` is invoked because the index already exists (and with different shard/replica settings at that).
Suggested fixes (pick one):
- Delete the index at the start of `createLtrIndex` (or in an `@After` method) before creating it.
- Use a unique index name per test (e.g., include the shard/replica counts in the name).
- Add an `@After` method that deletes the index so each test starts from a clean state.

@benwtrent The most straightforward patch is to add a rewrite step to the execution of the fetch phase but it feels like a huge change that will impact a lot of request.

WDYT? (cc @jimczi)

Adding rewrite to all fetch's seems really expensive. Though, traditionally, queries should all be rewritten already to semi-primitive forms, so maybe it isn't so bad? 

LTR is unique in that its rewrite is used to fetch a local reference to a model as serializing the model over the wire (which can be megabytes in size) is very expensive.

I wonder if ltr rescore can add additional metadata to the long lived context if explain is used?

> Adding rewrite to all fetch's seems really expensive. Though, traditionally, queries should all be rewritten already to semi-primitive forms, so maybe it isn't so bad?

I think it's fine, the query is already rewritten at this point so that shouldn't add any overhead. Also, if rewrite and fetch is applicable to the fetch phase then we should call it unconditionally. So +1 to just add a call to `rewriteAndFetchShardRequest` on the fetch phase, it will be a noop most of the time anyway.
OK folks, `rewriteAndFetchShardRequest` is now always called during the fetch phase as @jim suggested that the overhead should be very small.
